author: bryclevgp
title: [DATA-2640] Add ACS demographics to the district census layer for Serve
body:
Ticket: [DATA-2640](https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2b5524)

Serve is adding a view of how representative the constituents an official heard from are: where outreach respondents live, compared against the census makeup of the official's district. The ACS 2020-2024 block-group estimates and the block allocation already exist, and `district_census_stats` already says its ACS demographic layer would append at its grain. This fills that in and exposes what gp-api needs, so respondents and the district are compared on the same census source.

- **`district_census_stats` gains `acs_*` counts.** Local rows allocate block-group counts by the district's share of each block group's 2020 population, with the block group's full population (zero-voter blocks included) as the denominator, so a block group only partly inside a district type gives that district only its part. Statewide rows use the published state values. Counts only, since medians cannot be allocated, plus `acs_coverage_share` for districts with block groups the ACS does not publish. Point estimates: carrying margins through the allocation needs a variance model this layer does not have.
- **`gp_api_block_group_census_demographics`** exposes the same counts per block group, which gp-api uses to weight each respondent's home block group.
- **`Residence_Census_Block_Group_Geoid`** on `gp_api_voters` (from the L2 complete census geocode) and on consumer-only people (from `geocode_full`), so it flows through `gp_api_constituents`.

## Fixes since the first CI run

- **The CI failure.** `assert_district_census_demographics_block_group_shares_bounded` failed 120 rows and skipped everything downstream of the allocation. Every failure was rounding: `allocated_population` is `decimal(38,6)`, so summing 20 to 50 rounded rows per block group overshoots by 2 to 4 millionths against a 1e-6 tolerance. The bound is already implied by `assert_district_census_allocation_mass_conservation`, so the test is removed. `assert_district_census_stats_acs_race_sums_to_universe` is removed for the same reason: staging asserts the six groups sum exactly to their universe, and one loop applies the same share to every column.
- **Connecticut had no ACS demographics.** The 2020-2024 ACS codes CT block groups under planning regions (`091xx`). The decennial blocks and 96.5% of L2's CT geocodes use the 2020 county codes (`090xx`), so no CT block group matched. All 1,027 CT local districts would have published null `acs_*` with coverage 0, and CT voters' block-group key would not have joined the new table. `int__census_acs_demographics` now relabels CT block groups to 2020 codes through the staged Census crosswalk (new pass-through `stg_census_acs__ct_block_to_planning_region_2022`). The relabel is one-to-one at block-group grain (2,712 to 2,712; the 5 ACS block groups it cannot reach are unpopulated water), so no counts move and `gp_api_voters` needs no change.

## Verification

Dev build of the modified models, 60 of 60 nodes pass.

- `district_census_stats`: 110,791 rows in dev and prod, and 0 rows differ on the existing columns.
- Connecticut: 1,027 local districts, 0 below 0.99 coverage.
- Coverage below 0.995: 14 NY districts (the known Suffolk County publication hole, the same 14 the ACS design measured) and 50 zero-population districts with nothing to cover.
- ACS over 2020 decennial population, fully covered local districts with 1,000+ people: p01 0.79, p50 1.00, p99 1.26. CT p50 is 1.005.
- Race groups vs universe, the removed test replayed: 0 districts off by more than 1%.
- Voter key: 99.95% of geocoded voters outside CT and 99.88% in CT find their block group in `gp_api_block_group_census_demographics`. CT was about 0.1% before the remap.

## Deploy notes

- The voter column means the on-merge run full-refreshes `gp_api_voters` (tagged monthly, about 5 hours), then `gp_api_consumer_only_people` and `gp_api_constituents`. CI excludes the monthly tag, so the voter column is first built on merge. Merging away from the 00:02 and 12:02 UTC nightly runs avoids contention on shared tables.
- gp-api reads only `district_population` from `gp_api_district_census_stats` today, and the representation view still runs on sampled data, so the new columns break no reader.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+++ b/dbt/project/models/intermediate/civics/int__census_acs_demographics.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+-- ACS demographic counts at the two grains the district layer reads: block group
+-- (150), allocated into districts, and state (040), used whole for statewide rows.
+-- Counts only, so every column stays additive under allocation. The published
+-- medians are left out because a median cannot be allocated. Income is collapsed
+-- from sixteen published brackets into the six bands the product shows; a band is
+-- null when any of its brackets is suppressed, matching the staging rule.
+-- The ACS codes Connecticut under planning regions while decennial blocks and L2
+-- geocodes keep the 2020 county codes, so CT block groups are relabelled to 2020
+-- codes (one-to-one at this grain) for every downstream prefix join to match. The
+-- few the crosswalk cannot reach are unpopulated water.
+with
+    ct_block_groups as (
+        select distinct
+            left(block_geoid_2022, 12) as geoid_2022,
+            left(block_geoid_2020, 12) as geoid_2020
+        from {{ ref("stg_census_acs__ct_block_to_planning_region_2022") }}
+    )
+
+select
+    summary_level,
+    coalesce(ct_block_groups.geoid_2020, acs.geoid) as geoid,
+    total_population,
+    population_under_18,
+    population_65_plus,
+    population_race_universe,
+    population_white_nh,
+    population_black_nh,
+    population_native_american_nh,
+    population_asian_nh,
+    population_other_nh,
+    population_hispanic,
+    population_25_plus,
+    population_hs_or_higher,
+    population_bachelors_or_higher,
+    households,
+    owner_occupied_households,
+    population_poverty_universe,
+    population_below_poverty,
+    households_income_universe,
+    households_income_under_10k
+    + households_income_10k_to_15k
+    + households_income_15k_to_20k
+    + households_income_20k_to_25k as households_income_under_25k,
+    households_income_25k_to_30k
+    + households_income_30k_to_35k
+    + households_income_35k_to_40k
+    + households_income_40k_to_45k
+    + households_income_45k_to_50k as households_income_25k_to_50k,
+    households_income_50k_to_60k
+    + households_income_60k_to_75k as households_income_50k_to_75k,
+    households_income_75k_to_100k,
+    households_income_100k_to_125k
+    + households_income_125k_to_150k as households_income_100k_to_150k,
+    households_income_150k_to_200k
+    + households_income_200k_plus as households_income_150k_plus
+from {{ ref("stg_census_acs__geo_estimates") }} as acs
+left join ct_block_groups on acs.geoid = ct_block_groups.geoid_2022
+where summary_level in ('150', '040')

+  - name: int__census_acs_demographics
+    description: >
+      ACS 2020-2024 5-year demographic counts at block group (summary level 150) and
+      state (040), the two grains the district layer reads. Counts only so every column
+      stays additive under allocation; the published medians are left out. Household
+      income is collapsed from sixteen published brackets into six bands. Read by
+      int__district_census_demographics, district_census_stats (statewide rows), and
+      gp_api_block_group_census_demographics.

+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+          - accepted_values:
+              arguments:
+                values: ["150", "040"]
+      - name: geoid

+          12-digit block group geoid under 2020 county codes (Connecticut included),
+          or 2-digit state FIPS.
+        data_tests:
+          - not_null
+
+  - name: int__district_census_demographics
+    description: >
+      ACS demographic counts for each local district: block-group counts multiplied by
+      the district's share of the block group's 2020 census population, then summed.
+      The share's denominator is the block group's full population (zero-voter blocks
+      included), so a block group only partly inside a district type gives the district
+      only its part. Point estimates; margins are not carried. One row per
+      (state_postal_code, district_type, district_name), the same key as
+      int__district_population.
+    data_tests:
+      - dbt_utils.unique_combination_of_columns:
+          arguments:
+            combination_of_columns: [state_postal_code, district_type, district_name]
+    columns:

@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+{%- set acs_counts = [
+    "total_population",
+    "population_under_18",
+    "population_65_plus",
+    "population_race_universe",
+    "population_white_nh",
+    "population_black_nh",
+    "population_native_american_nh",
+    "population_asian_nh",
+    "population_other_nh",
+    "population_hispanic",
+    "population_25_plus",
+    "population_hs_or_higher",
+    "population_bachelors_or_higher",
+    "households",
+    "owner_occupied_households",
+    "population_poverty_universe",
+    "population_below_poverty",
+    "households_income_universe",
+    "households_income_under_25k",
+    "households_income_25k_to_50k",
+    "households_income_50k_to_75k",
+    "households_income_75k_to_100k",
+    "households_income_100k_to_150k",
+    "households_income_150k_plus",
+] -%}
+
+-- ACS demographics for each local district: block-group counts allocated by the
+-- district's share of the block group's population. The share's denominator is the
+-- block group's full 2020 census population, zero-voter blocks included, so a
+-- block group that is only partly inside a district's type (a city edge, say)
+-- gives the district only its part rather than all of it.
+-- Shares come from 2020 decennial population and are applied to ACS 2020-2024
+-- counts: a ratio, so the vintage mismatch moves magnitudes, not shares.
+-- Margins are not carried; allocating them needs a variance model this layer does
+-- not have, so these are point estimates.
+with
+    allocation as (select * from {{ ref("int__district_census_allocation") }}),
+
+    block_group_population as (
+        select
+            left(block_geoid, 12) as block_group_geoid,
+            sum(population) as block_group_population
+        from {{ ref("stg_census__block_population") }}
+        group by left(block_geoid, 12)
+    ),
+
+    district_block_groups as (
+        select
+            state_postal_code,
+            district_type,
+            district_name,
+            block_group_geoid,
+            sum(allocated_population) as allocated_population
+        from allocation
+        group by state_postal_code, district_type, district_name, block_group_geoid
+    ),
+
+    shares as (
+        select
+            district_block_groups.*,
+            district_block_groups.allocated_population
+            / block_group_population.block_group_population as block_group_share
+        from district_block_groups
+        inner join
+            block_group_population
+            on district_block_groups.block_group_geoid
+            = block_group_population.block_group_geoid
+        where block_group_population.block_group_population > 0
+    ),
+
+    acs as (
+        select *
+        from {{ ref("int__census_acs_demographics") }}
+        where summary_level = '150'
+    )
+
+select
+    shares.state_postal_code,
+    shares.district_type,
+    shares.district_name,
+    {%- for column in acs_counts %}
+        sum(shares.block_group_share * acs.{{ column }}) as acs_{{ column }},
+    {%- endfor %}
+    -- Share of the district's allocated population living in block groups with a
+    -- published ACS total. Below 1 means unpublished block groups left counts out.
+    coalesce(
+        sum(
+            case
+                when acs.total_population is not null then shares.allocated_population
+            end
+        )
+        / nullif(sum(shares.allocated_population), 0),
+        0
+    ) as acs_coverage_share
+from shares
+left join acs on shares.block_group_geoid = acs.geoid
+group by shares.state_postal_code, shares.district_type, shares.district_name

     allocation as (select * from {{ ref("int__district_census_allocation") }}),

             sp.state_postal_code,
@@ -81,9 +126,29 @@ with
             sp.state_postal_code as district_name,
             sp.district_population,

-            coalesce(sv.registered_voters, 0) as registered_voters

         from statewide_pop sp
         left join statewide_voters sv using (state_postal_code)
+        left join statewide_acs sa using (state_postal_code)

+        select
+            ld.state_postal_code,

+            coalesce(dd.acs_coverage_share, 0) as acs_coverage_share
+        from local_districts ld
+        left join

     )
 
 select
@@ -92,8 +157,10 @@ select
     district_name,

priorFindings.body: The `dbt_expectations.expect_column_values_to_match_regex` test on `Residence_Census_Block_Group_Geoid` has no null guard, but the column description explicitly states it is "Null when L2 has no geocode for the address." Elsewhere in this project, the same test type on nullable columns consistently adds an explicit null exclusion (e.g. `__sources.yaml` uses `config: where: "race_name is not null"` for the same test macro on other nullable columns). If the installed dbt_expectations fork does not auto-skip nulls, this test will fail on every CI run with real L2 data containing voters without a geocode.
